"**The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)**" is a [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music")-[pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") song written by [Otha Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otha_Young "Otha Young") for [Juice Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton "Juice Newton") in the mid-1970s. Newton was known for charting hits on the Hot 100, Adult Contemporary, and Hot Country charts - and this song has the distinction of being the only single of hers to reach the top 10 on all three of those charts, peaking at #1 on both the Adult Contemporary and the Hot Country charts.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Sweetest_Thing_(I%27ve_Ever_Known)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

"The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)" was originally recorded and released in 1975 on Juice Newton & Silver Spur's debut album, _[Juice Newton and Silver Spur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice\_Newton\_&\_Silver\_Spur\_(album) "Juice Newton & Silver Spur (album)")_ ([RCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Corporation "RCA Corporation")). The 1975 version was not issued as a single, although it was the B-side of two official singles and was issued as a promotional single to U.S. radio stations. In the meantime, [Dottsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dottsy "Dottsy") recorded a version in 1976 and took it to No. 86 on the country music charts and used it as the title track to her album _The Sweetest Thing_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-whitburn-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-Hyatt-2)

After becoming a solo artist, Newton re-recorded the song for her 1981 album, the star-making _[Juice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice\_(Juice\_Newton\_album) "Juice (Juice Newton album)")_, which was Newton's third solo album and featured three of her biggest pop hits: "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)", "[Angel of the Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_of_the_Morning "Angel of the Morning")" and "[Queen of Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_Hearts_(Hank_DeVito_song) "Queen of Hearts (Hank DeVito song)")".

In early 1982, "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)" reached No. 1 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[adult contemporary chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Adult_Contemporary_Tracks "Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-Hyatt-2) No. 1 on the _Billboard_[country chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-Hyatt-2) and No. 7 on the _Billboard_[pop chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100"), where it remained in the [Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_40 "Top 40") for eighteen weeks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-3) The single is the only of Juice Newton's to reach the Top 10 on all three charts. On Billboard's year-end Top 40 chart, the song charted at No. 21 of all the singles of 1982. The music video for the song was filmed in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").

The first pressings of the _Juice_ album featured a different arrangement of the song, with a more prominent steel guitar part and no oboe. After the unexpected crossover success of "Angel of the Morning" and "Queen of Hearts", a pop version was mixed and replaced the country version on all future pressings of the album. The revamped version was also used for the single (which, somewhat ironically, became her first No. 1 Country Single). The 1981 country version can be found on the United Kingdom best-of CD _Country Classics_ and BGO's two-CD "Juice/Quiet Lies/Dirty Looks" boxed set.

"**The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)**" is a [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music")-[pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") song written by [Otha Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otha_Young "Otha Young") for [Juice Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton "Juice Newton") in the mid-1970s. Newton was known for charting hits on the Hot 100, Adult Contemporary, and Hot Country charts - and this song has the distinction of being the only single of hers to reach the top 10 on all three of those charts, peaking at #1 on both the Adult Contemporary and the Hot Country charts.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Sweetest_Thing_(I%27ve_Ever_Known)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

"The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)" was originally recorded and released in 1975 on Juice Newton & Silver Spur's debut album, _[Juice Newton and Silver Spur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice\_Newton\_&\_Silver\_Spur\_(album) "Juice Newton & Silver Spur (album)")_ ([RCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Corporation "RCA Corporation")). The 1975 version was not issued as a single, although it was the B-side of two official singles and was issued as a promotional single to U.S. radio stations. In the meantime, [Dottsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dottsy "Dottsy") recorded a version in 1976 and took it to No. 86 on the country music charts and used it as the title track to her album _The Sweetest Thing_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-whitburn-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-Hyatt-2)

After becoming a solo artist, Newton re-recorded the song for her 1981 album, the star-making _[Juice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice\_(Juice\_Newton\_album) "Juice (Juice Newton album)")_, which was Newton's third solo album and featured three of her biggest pop hits: "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)", "[Angel of the Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_of_the_Morning "Angel of the Morning")" and "[Queen of Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_Hearts_(Hank_DeVito_song) "Queen of Hearts (Hank DeVito song)")".

In early 1982, "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)" reached No. 1 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[adult contemporary chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Adult_Contemporary_Tracks "Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-Hyatt-2) No. 1 on the _Billboard_[country chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-Hyatt-2) and No. 7 on the _Billboard_[pop chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100"), where it remained in the [Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_40 "Top 40") for eighteen weeks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known)#cite_note-3) The single is the only of Juice Newton's to reach the Top 10 on all three charts. On Billboard's year-end Top 40 chart, the song charted at No. 21 of all the singles of 1982. The music video for the song was filmed in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").

The first pressings of the _Juice_ album featured a different arrangement of the song, with a more prominent steel guitar part and no oboe. After the unexpected crossover success of "Angel of the Morning" and "Queen of Hearts", a pop version was mixed and replaced the country version on all future pressings of the album. The revamped version was also used for the single (which, somewhat ironically, became her first No. 1 Country Single). The 1981 country version can be found on the United Kingdom best-of CD _Country Classics_ and BGO's two-CD "Juice/Quiet Lies/Dirty Looks" boxed set.

_**Mallrats**_ is a 1995 American [buddy comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_comedy_film "Buddy comedy film") written and directed by [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith"). The film stars [Shannen Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty "Shannen Doherty"), [Jeremy London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_London "Jeremy London"), [Jason Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Lee "Jason Lee"), [Claire Forlani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claire_Forlani "Claire Forlani"), [Priscilla Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priscilla_Barnes "Priscilla Barnes"), and [Michael Rooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Rooker "Michael Rooker"). It is the second film in the [View Askewniverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/View_Askewniverse "View Askewniverse"). The film follows two best friends as they retreat to a local mall after being dumped by their girlfriends on the same day.

_Mallrats_ had its premiere at the Cineplex Odeon Universal City Cinemas in [Universal City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_City,_California "Universal City, California") on October 19, 1995, and was released in the United States on October 20 by [Gramercy Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramercy_Pictures "Gramercy Pictures"). The film received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $2.1 million against a $6.1 million budget. It has since garnered a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-3)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

College student T.S. Quint is preparing for a trip to [Universal Studios Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_Florida "Universal Studios Florida") in [Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida") with Brandi Svenning, during which he plans to propose to her; however, Brandi tells him she cannot go due to having volunteered to fill in as a contestant on _Truth or Date_, her father's [dating game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dating_game_show "Dating game show"), because the original contestant had died from an embolism bursting in her brain while swimming 700 laps at the local Y.M.C.A. following T.S.'s comment regarding her weight. Brandi and T.S. argue over his responsibility and the two break up. T.S. turns to his best friend [Brodie Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brodie_Bruce "Brodie Bruce"), who has been dumped by his girlfriend Rene, and Brodie suggests the two might find comfort at the local mall.

Brodie and T.S. discover _Truth or Date_ is being filmed at the same mall, through their friend Willam, who throughout the film tries to see a sailboat in a [Magic Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Eye "Magic Eye") poster. The two ask local [slackers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slacker "Slacker")[Jay and Silent Bob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_and_Silent_Bob "Jay and Silent Bob") to destroy the show's stage, a task for which they devise elaborate but ultimately unsuccessful plans. Brodie and T.S. run into Tricia Jones, a 15-year-old senior who is writing a book on the sex drive of men ages 14–30, for which she has sex with various men as research and films every encounter. She then reveals that the previous night she had sex with Shannon Hamilton, a 25-year-old clothing-store manager who hates Brodie because of his "lack of a shopping agenda".

Brodie then learns that Rene has begun a relationship with Shannon. Brodie confronts Rene to find out more about the relationship, and the two have sex in an elevator. Brodie is later accosted and attacked by Shannon, who intends to have anal sex with Rene. As a result of this incident, Jay and Silent Bob assault the mall's [Easter Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Bunny "Easter Bunny"), under the incorrect assumption that he attacked Brodie.

Brandi's father Jared has Brodie and T.S. arrested on false charges of drug possession at the mall. Jay and Silent Bob are able to rescue Brodie and T.S., and they hide out at a local [flea market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_market "Flea market"). There, they encounter Ivannah, a topless fortune teller with three nipples, who offers advice on their relationship problems. While Brodie is visibly uncomfortable with the situation, T.S. pays close attention to Ivannah's advice and decides to win Brandi back. Eventually, the two return to the mall.

Before the show begins, Brodie meets famed [Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") legend [Stan Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Lee "Stan Lee"), who gives him advice on romance. After this, Brodie requests that his friend Tricia Jones retrieve footage of her having sex with Shannon. Meanwhile, T.S. also persuades Jay to get two of the game show contestants stoned, which allows him and Brodie to replace them on _Truth or Date_.

During the show, Brandi recognizes the voices of Brodie and T.S., leading to an on-air argument between them. Brodie eventually intervenes, explaining that T.S. has spent the entire day pining for Brandi. Subsequently, T.S. proposes to Brandi, who accepts. After the show concludes and as the police arrive to arrest T.S. and Brodie, Silent Bob broadcasts a sex tape featuring Shannon and Tricia. This leads to Shannon's arrest for [statutory rape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statutory_rape "Statutory rape"). In the extended cut, Jared is arrested for 19 [FCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FCC "FCC") violations and broadcasting lewd or indecent images in a public forum. Consequently, Brodie and Rene rekindle their relationship.

The conclusion reveals that T.S. marries Brandi at Universal Studios while on a [Jaws attraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(ride) "Jaws (ride)"), Tricia's book is a bestseller, Shannon is imprisoned (and subsequently raped), Willam eventually does see the sailboat, Brodie becomes the host of _[The Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show "The Tonight Show")_ (with Rene as his bandleader), and that Jay and Silent Bob get an [orangutan named Susanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_and_Silent_Bob_Strike_Back "Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back").

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

After the success of the independent hit _Clerks_, writer/director Kevin Smith and his best friend/producer Scott Mosier began to make their second film. After a screening of _Clerks_, producer [James Jacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jacks "James Jacks") approached them to do another film for [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"). Smith soon finished the script for _Mallrats_, and casting began.

[Jeremy London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_London "Jeremy London"), an actor with a TV series and a few films to his credit, was cast as T.S.; [Henry Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Thomas "Henry Thomas") was the finalist of the role.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Shannen Doherty was the most famous cast member after her appearances in several films and the hit TV show _[Beverly Hills, 90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly\_Hills,\_90210 "Beverly Hills, 90210")_. [Jason Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Lee_(actor) "Jason Lee (actor)") was cast with no prior acting experience; before the film, Lee was a professional skateboarder, and [Adam Sandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Sandler "Adam Sandler") and [Steve Zahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Zahn "Steve Zahn") were the finalists for the role of Brodie Bruce.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck"), who was a relative unknown at the time, was cast as Shannon Hamilton. [Joey Lauren Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Lauren_Adams "Joey Lauren Adams") was cast as Gwen Turner; she later dated Smith, and during that time, he wrote the main character in _[Chasing Amy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chasing\_Amy "Chasing Amy")_ for her. Ethan Suplee was cast as Willam Black. [Scott Mosier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Mosier "Scott Mosier") was supposed to reprise the role, but Smith and the film's producers were so impressed with Suplee that they cast him, instead.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The most troublesome role to cast was Jay, as Universal did not want [Jason Mewes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Mewes "Jason Mewes") to have the role, despite playing him in _Clerks_ and the character being based on him. Mewes had to audition for the part against actors [Seth Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Green "Seth Green") and [Breckin Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breckin_Meyer "Breckin Meyer").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-4) Smith also said that he wrote the role of Jared Svenning for [William Atherton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Atherton "William Atherton"), but Atherton did not want to be [typecast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typecasting "Typecasting").

Smith wanted to shoot the film in [Seaview Square Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seaview_Square_Mall "Seaview Square Mall") in [Ocean Township, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Township,_Monmouth_County,_New_Jersey "Ocean Township, Monmouth County, New Jersey"); however, due to lower production costs, it was filmed at [Eden Prairie Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Prairie_Center "Eden Prairie Center") mall in [Eden Prairie, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Prairie,_Minnesota "Eden Prairie, Minnesota") instead.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-5)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")]

The film grossed $400,000 on its Friday opening on 800 screens, $1.2 million on its opening weekend, and grossed an overall total of $2,122,561 at the box office.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-mojo-1)

_Mallrats_ was the subject of much critical derision when it was released, with many critics comparing it unfavorably to Smith's first film, _Clerks_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-6) In his negative review of the film, critic [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") gave the film 1 1/2 stars out of 4 and said "Before _Mallrats_ was released, I chaired a panel that Smith participated in and Kevin Smith cheerfully said he'd be happy to do whatever the studios wanted, if they'd pay for his films. At the time, I thought he was joking."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-7) On their television program _[Siskel & Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At\_the\_Movies\_(1986\_TV\_program) "At the Movies (1986 TV program)")_, Ebert's colleague [Gene Siskel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Siskel "Gene Siskel") said, "I sat stonefaced throughout _Mallrats_, not laughing once. I couldn't believe it was the same talent involved that made _Clerks_." He deemed the jokes "stale and recycled" and recommended moviegoers rent _Clerks_ instead of seeing _Mallrats_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-8)

On [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator")[Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film has an approval rating of 58% based on 48 reviews, with an average rating of 5.6/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_Mallrats_ colorfully expands the View Askewniverse, even if its snootchie has lost a few of the bootchies boasted by its beloved predecessor."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-9) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film received a score of 41 based on 18 reviews, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-10)

In 2020, Arrow Video released a 25th anniversary Blu-Ray that contains a third "television cut" of the film, with many scenes altered and re-dubbed to remove profanity.

### Extended cut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Extended cut")]

The extended cut contains over 30 minutes of additional footage and subplots.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-12) They include:

*   An alternate opening scene, in which Mr. Svenning hosts a Ball for the Governor of New Jersey (played by [Elizabeth Ashley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Ashley "Elizabeth Ashley")). In this scene, T.S. (dressed as a colonial musketeer) accidentally gets his musket tangled up in Brandi's hair, then accidentally shoots at the Governor on the roof of a school, which ends up costing Mr. Svenning his reputation as well as a big pay raise. This explains the reason why Svenning shows an intense dislike for T.S. and why Brandi is so intent on breaking up with him. This scene also makes no mention of Julie Dwyer's death, as the theatrical cut did. (That cut subplot was referenced in the final cut of the movie, where the TV execs mention to Svenning that they do not want a repeat of the Governor's Ball.)
*   Multiple lines throughout the movie are restored, related to T.S.'s "attempted assassination" of the governor. Many of these have wildly different reasons for having seen T.S. on the news, such as Shannon's claim that he had tried to kidnap the President's daughter.
*   An extended sequence at Brodie's house, where T.S. is hounded by the media as a result of his actions at the Governor's Ball, including several TV movie offers.
*   Included scenes where T.S. also makes it known to Brandi that he proposed to marry her.
*   A scene in which Brodie and T.S. arrive outside of Mr. Svenning's home, so T.S. can try and reconcile, and during the confusion, thanks to a news crew chasing T.S., then interviewing Brodie (who then implies that Mr. Svenning and Brandi take part in [Satanic rituals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Mass "Black Mass")), the news crew records footage of Svenning doing martial arts in a bath-towel. (Some of the footage of Mr. Svenning was re-edited in the theatrical release into the new intro.)
*   A shot that shows the Quick Stop from _Clerks_.
*   A new subplot of Brodie showing intentions of wanting to be on television, which explains his surprised look during his appearance on _Truth or Date_.
*   An extended arrest scene in which LaFours wants to put Brodie and T.S. into jail for an extended period of time, rather than "overnight" when the pair were initially arrested.
*   An extended fight scene between Brodie and Shannon Hamilton
*   A scene after _Truth or Date_ in which Mr. Svenning demands to have T.S. and Brodie arrested, but instead he is the one who is arrested. It turns out that since Svenning was the producer of the show, he faces multiple FCC fines for Brodie's antics.
*   An extended "Where are they now?" ending sequence, in which Mr. Svenning is shown at his job at the network as a janitor (along with his production assistant, still wearing his headset), and Shannon Hamilton is shown screaming after his rape in prison.
*   A scene that showed Tricia flirting and having sex with LaFours in order to distract him from catching Jay and Silent Bob.

As explained by Kevin Smith in the introduction, most of the scenes were reworked because of the test audience's negative reaction. Some of the dialogue had been re-dubbed in the theatrical release, but is restored in this version; extended scenes have notable [jump cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_cut "Jump cut").

## Sequel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Sequel")]

On March 13, 2015, Smith confirmed that _Mallrats 2_ was being written and was slated to begin shooting in summer 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Filming-announcement-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Shoot-Change-14) In April 2015, Smith announced that _Mallrats 2_ would be his next film, instead of _[Clerks III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerks\_III "Clerks III")_ as originally intended, and would begin filming in 2015.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Shoot-Change-14) From April 2015 to July 2016, Smith made a series of announcements regarding the proposed sequel, some regarding casting and some announcing delays in production.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-15) During this time, the planned film became a planned 10-episode television miniseries.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-TV-Series-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Mallbrats-tv-series-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-18)

In February 2017, Smith announced that pitches to six different networks resulted in no one willing to produce the TV series, but expressed his hope that interest in the series would spike after the release of the film _[Jay and Silent Bob Reboot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay\_and\_Silent\_Bob\_Reboot "Jay and Silent Bob Reboot")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-19)

In January 2020, Smith announced that development on a _Mallrats_ sequel film had started up again, under a new title, _Twilight of the Mallrats_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-21) On April 24, Smith stated that he had completed the first draft of the script and that the original cast would return.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-22) On May 12, 2020, Smith revealed that [Aparna Brielle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aparna_Brielle "Aparna Brielle"), who played Jihad in _Jay and Silent Bob Reboot_, had been set to lead the film as Banner, the daughter of Brodie, and that Doherty would return to reprise her role of Rene Mosier.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-23)

Doherty died on July 13, 2024.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-24) A few months later, however, Smith suggested that the sequel could still be made, reframed as a tribute to Doherty, with her friend [Sarah Michelle Gellar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Michelle_Gellar "Sarah Michelle Gellar")—who had auditioned for a role in the original _Mallrats_—"step[ping] in for" her. In an [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") comment, Gellar expressed support for the idea.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-25)

_**Mallrats**_ is a 1995 American [buddy comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_comedy_film "Buddy comedy film") written and directed by [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith"). The film stars [Shannen Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty "Shannen Doherty"), [Jeremy London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_London "Jeremy London"), [Jason Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Lee "Jason Lee"), [Claire Forlani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claire_Forlani "Claire Forlani"), [Priscilla Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priscilla_Barnes "Priscilla Barnes"), and [Michael Rooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Rooker "Michael Rooker"). It is the second film in the [View Askewniverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/View_Askewniverse "View Askewniverse"). The film follows two best friends as they retreat to a local mall after being dumped by their girlfriends on the same day.

_Mallrats_ had its premiere at the Cineplex Odeon Universal City Cinemas in [Universal City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_City,_California "Universal City, California") on October 19, 1995, and was released in the United States on October 20 by [Gramercy Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramercy_Pictures "Gramercy Pictures"). The film received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $2.1 million against a $6.1 million budget. It has since garnered a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-3)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

College student T.S. Quint is preparing for a trip to [Universal Studios Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_Florida "Universal Studios Florida") in [Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida") with Brandi Svenning, during which he plans to propose to her; however, Brandi tells him she cannot go due to having volunteered to fill in as a contestant on _Truth or Date_, her father's [dating game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dating_game_show "Dating game show"), because the original contestant had died from an embolism bursting in her brain while swimming 700 laps at the local Y.M.C.A. following T.S.'s comment regarding her weight. Brandi and T.S. argue over his responsibility and the two break up. T.S. turns to his best friend [Brodie Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brodie_Bruce "Brodie Bruce"), who has been dumped by his girlfriend Rene, and Brodie suggests the two might find comfort at the local mall.

Brodie and T.S. discover _Truth or Date_ is being filmed at the same mall, through their friend Willam, who throughout the film tries to see a sailboat in a [Magic Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Eye "Magic Eye") poster. The two ask local [slackers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slacker "Slacker")[Jay and Silent Bob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_and_Silent_Bob "Jay and Silent Bob") to destroy the show's stage, a task for which they devise elaborate but ultimately unsuccessful plans. Brodie and T.S. run into Tricia Jones, a 15-year-old senior who is writing a book on the sex drive of men ages 14–30, for which she has sex with various men as research and films every encounter. She then reveals that the previous night she had sex with Shannon Hamilton, a 25-year-old clothing-store manager who hates Brodie because of his "lack of a shopping agenda".

Brodie then learns that Rene has begun a relationship with Shannon. Brodie confronts Rene to find out more about the relationship, and the two have sex in an elevator. Brodie is later accosted and attacked by Shannon, who intends to have anal sex with Rene. As a result of this incident, Jay and Silent Bob assault the mall's [Easter Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Bunny "Easter Bunny"), under the incorrect assumption that he attacked Brodie.

Brandi's father Jared has Brodie and T.S. arrested on false charges of drug possession at the mall. Jay and Silent Bob are able to rescue Brodie and T.S., and they hide out at a local [flea market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_market "Flea market"). There, they encounter Ivannah, a topless fortune teller with three nipples, who offers advice on their relationship problems. While Brodie is visibly uncomfortable with the situation, T.S. pays close attention to Ivannah's advice and decides to win Brandi back. Eventually, the two return to the mall.

Before the show begins, Brodie meets famed [Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") legend [Stan Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Lee "Stan Lee"), who gives him advice on romance. After this, Brodie requests that his friend Tricia Jones retrieve footage of her having sex with Shannon. Meanwhile, T.S. also persuades Jay to get two of the game show contestants stoned, which allows him and Brodie to replace them on _Truth or Date_.

During the show, Brandi recognizes the voices of Brodie and T.S., leading to an on-air argument between them. Brodie eventually intervenes, explaining that T.S. has spent the entire day pining for Brandi. Subsequently, T.S. proposes to Brandi, who accepts. After the show concludes and as the police arrive to arrest T.S. and Brodie, Silent Bob broadcasts a sex tape featuring Shannon and Tricia. This leads to Shannon's arrest for [statutory rape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statutory_rape "Statutory rape"). In the extended cut, Jared is arrested for 19 [FCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FCC "FCC") violations and broadcasting lewd or indecent images in a public forum. Consequently, Brodie and Rene rekindle their relationship.

The conclusion reveals that T.S. marries Brandi at Universal Studios while on a [Jaws attraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(ride) "Jaws (ride)"), Tricia's book is a bestseller, Shannon is imprisoned (and subsequently raped), Willam eventually does see the sailboat, Brodie becomes the host of _[The Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show "The Tonight Show")_ (with Rene as his bandleader), and that Jay and Silent Bob get an [orangutan named Susanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_and_Silent_Bob_Strike_Back "Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back").

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

After the success of the independent hit _Clerks_, writer/director Kevin Smith and his best friend/producer Scott Mosier began to make their second film. After a screening of _Clerks_, producer [James Jacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jacks "James Jacks") approached them to do another film for [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"). Smith soon finished the script for _Mallrats_, and casting began.

[Jeremy London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_London "Jeremy London"), an actor with a TV series and a few films to his credit, was cast as T.S.; [Henry Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Thomas "Henry Thomas") was the finalist of the role.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Shannen Doherty was the most famous cast member after her appearances in several films and the hit TV show _[Beverly Hills, 90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly\_Hills,\_90210 "Beverly Hills, 90210")_. [Jason Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Lee_(actor) "Jason Lee (actor)") was cast with no prior acting experience; before the film, Lee was a professional skateboarder, and [Adam Sandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Sandler "Adam Sandler") and [Steve Zahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Zahn "Steve Zahn") were the finalists for the role of Brodie Bruce.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck"), who was a relative unknown at the time, was cast as Shannon Hamilton. [Joey Lauren Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Lauren_Adams "Joey Lauren Adams") was cast as Gwen Turner; she later dated Smith, and during that time, he wrote the main character in _[Chasing Amy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chasing\_Amy "Chasing Amy")_ for her. Ethan Suplee was cast as Willam Black. [Scott Mosier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Mosier "Scott Mosier") was supposed to reprise the role, but Smith and the film's producers were so impressed with Suplee that they cast him, instead.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The most troublesome role to cast was Jay, as Universal did not want [Jason Mewes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Mewes "Jason Mewes") to have the role, despite playing him in _Clerks_ and the character being based on him. Mewes had to audition for the part against actors [Seth Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Green "Seth Green") and [Breckin Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breckin_Meyer "Breckin Meyer").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-4) Smith also said that he wrote the role of Jared Svenning for [William Atherton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Atherton "William Atherton"), but Atherton did not want to be [typecast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typecasting "Typecasting").

Smith wanted to shoot the film in [Seaview Square Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seaview_Square_Mall "Seaview Square Mall") in [Ocean Township, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Township,_Monmouth_County,_New_Jersey "Ocean Township, Monmouth County, New Jersey"); however, due to lower production costs, it was filmed at [Eden Prairie Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Prairie_Center "Eden Prairie Center") mall in [Eden Prairie, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Prairie,_Minnesota "Eden Prairie, Minnesota") instead.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-5)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")]

The film grossed $400,000 on its Friday opening on 800 screens, $1.2 million on its opening weekend, and grossed an overall total of $2,122,561 at the box office.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-mojo-1)

_Mallrats_ was the subject of much critical derision when it was released, with many critics comparing it unfavorably to Smith's first film, _Clerks_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-6) In his negative review of the film, critic [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") gave the film 1 1/2 stars out of 4 and said "Before _Mallrats_ was released, I chaired a panel that Smith participated in and Kevin Smith cheerfully said he'd be happy to do whatever the studios wanted, if they'd pay for his films. At the time, I thought he was joking."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-7) On their television program _[Siskel & Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At\_the\_Movies\_(1986\_TV\_program) "At the Movies (1986 TV program)")_, Ebert's colleague [Gene Siskel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Siskel "Gene Siskel") said, "I sat stonefaced throughout _Mallrats_, not laughing once. I couldn't believe it was the same talent involved that made _Clerks_." He deemed the jokes "stale and recycled" and recommended moviegoers rent _Clerks_ instead of seeing _Mallrats_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-8)

On [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator")[Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film has an approval rating of 58% based on 48 reviews, with an average rating of 5.6/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "_Mallrats_ colorfully expands the View Askewniverse, even if its snootchie has lost a few of the bootchies boasted by its beloved predecessor."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-9) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film received a score of 41 based on 18 reviews, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-10)

## Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Home media ")]

In 1996, MCA/Universal Home Video released the movie on VHS and Laserdisc (the latter in widescreen format).

A [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") was released in 1999 including 1.85:1 Anamorphic widescreen picture & 5.1 Dolby surround sound (both of which the movie was in for the Laserdisc release). Bonus features include:[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-11)

*   [Audio commentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_commentary "Audio commentary") with director [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith"), cast members [Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck"), [Jason Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Lee_(actor) "Jason Lee (actor)"), and [Jason Mewes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Mewes "Jason Mewes"), and producers [Scott Mosier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Mosier "Scott Mosier")& Vincent Pereira
*   [Deleted scenes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deleted_scene "Deleted scene")
*   Featurette – _View Askew's Look Back at Mallrats_
*   Music video – _[Build Me Up Buttercup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build\_Me\_Up\_Buttercup "Build Me Up Buttercup")_ by The Goops (directed by Kevin Smith)
*   Cast and Filmmaker Bios
*   Theatrical trailer

In 2005, a 10th anniversary double-sided DVD was released, containing the original version of the film, features from the previous DVD release, and an all new extended cut of the movie.

The film was released on Blu-ray in 2014 and it used digital noise reduction and edge enhancement (as part of Universal's 1990's Best of the Decade collection); the menus were replaced with Universal-mandated menus, the [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features") logo replaced the Universal logo at the start of the film, and some copies also included a code for a digital streaming version to be redeemed at Universal's online [UltraViolet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UltraViolet_(system) "UltraViolet (system)") service, and [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes").

In 2020, Arrow Video released a 25th anniversary Blu-Ray that contains a third "television cut" of the film, with many scenes altered and re-dubbed to remove profanity.

### Extended cut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Extended cut")]

The extended cut contains over 30 minutes of additional footage and subplots.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-12) They include:

*   An alternate opening scene, in which Mr. Svenning hosts a Ball for the Governor of New Jersey (played by [Elizabeth Ashley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Ashley "Elizabeth Ashley")). In this scene, T.S. (dressed as a colonial musketeer) accidentally gets his musket tangled up in Brandi's hair, then accidentally shoots at the Governor on the roof of a school, which ends up costing Mr. Svenning his reputation as well as a big pay raise. This explains the reason why Svenning shows an intense dislike for T.S. and why Brandi is so intent on breaking up with him. This scene also makes no mention of Julie Dwyer's death, as the theatrical cut did. (That cut subplot was referenced in the final cut of the movie, where the TV execs mention to Svenning that they do not want a repeat of the Governor's Ball.)
*   Multiple lines throughout the movie are restored, related to T.S.'s "attempted assassination" of the governor. Many of these have wildly different reasons for having seen T.S. on the news, such as Shannon's claim that he had tried to kidnap the President's daughter.
*   An extended sequence at Brodie's house, where T.S. is hounded by the media as a result of his actions at the Governor's Ball, including several TV movie offers.
*   Included scenes where T.S. also makes it known to Brandi that he proposed to marry her.
*   A scene in which Brodie and T.S. arrive outside of Mr. Svenning's home, so T.S. can try and reconcile, and during the confusion, thanks to a news crew chasing T.S., then interviewing Brodie (who then implies that Mr. Svenning and Brandi take part in [Satanic rituals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Mass "Black Mass")), the news crew records footage of Svenning doing martial arts in a bath-towel. (Some of the footage of Mr. Svenning was re-edited in the theatrical release into the new intro.)
*   A shot that shows the Quick Stop from _Clerks_.
*   A new subplot of Brodie showing intentions of wanting to be on television, which explains his surprised look during his appearance on _Truth or Date_.
*   An extended arrest scene in which LaFours wants to put Brodie and T.S. into jail for an extended period of time, rather than "overnight" when the pair were initially arrested.
*   An extended fight scene between Brodie and Shannon Hamilton
*   A scene after _Truth or Date_ in which Mr. Svenning demands to have T.S. and Brodie arrested, but instead he is the one who is arrested. It turns out that since Svenning was the producer of the show, he faces multiple FCC fines for Brodie's antics.
*   An extended "Where are they now?" ending sequence, in which Mr. Svenning is shown at his job at the network as a janitor (along with his production assistant, still wearing his headset), and Shannon Hamilton is shown screaming after his rape in prison.
*   A scene that showed Tricia flirting and having sex with LaFours in order to distract him from catching Jay and Silent Bob.

As explained by Kevin Smith in the introduction, most of the scenes were reworked because of the test audience's negative reaction. Some of the dialogue had been re-dubbed in the theatrical release, but is restored in this version; extended scenes have notable [jump cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_cut "Jump cut").

## Sequel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mallrats&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Sequel")]

On March 13, 2015, Smith confirmed that _Mallrats 2_ was being written and was slated to begin shooting in summer 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Filming-announcement-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Shoot-Change-14) In April 2015, Smith announced that _Mallrats 2_ would be his next film, instead of _[Clerks III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerks\_III "Clerks III")_ as originally intended, and would begin filming in 2015.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Shoot-Change-14) From April 2015 to July 2016, Smith made a series of announcements regarding the proposed sequel, some regarding casting and some announcing delays in production.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-15) During this time, the planned film became a planned 10-episode television miniseries.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-TV-Series-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-Mallbrats-tv-series-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-18)

In February 2017, Smith announced that pitches to six different networks resulted in no one willing to produce the TV series, but expressed his hope that interest in the series would spike after the release of the film _[Jay and Silent Bob Reboot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay\_and\_Silent\_Bob\_Reboot "Jay and Silent Bob Reboot")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-19)

In January 2020, Smith announced that development on a _Mallrats_ sequel film had started up again, under a new title, _Twilight of the Mallrats_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-21) On April 24, Smith stated that he had completed the first draft of the script and that the original cast would return.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-22) On May 12, 2020, Smith revealed that [Aparna Brielle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aparna_Brielle "Aparna Brielle"), who played Jihad in _Jay and Silent Bob Reboot_, had been set to lead the film as Banner, the daughter of Brodie, and that Doherty would return to reprise her role of Rene Mosier.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-23)

Doherty died on July 13, 2024.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-24) A few months later, however, Smith suggested that the sequel could still be made, reframed as a tribute to Doherty, with her friend [Sarah Michelle Gellar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Michelle_Gellar "Sarah Michelle Gellar")—who had auditioned for a role in the original _Mallrats_—"step[ping] in for" her. In an [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") comment, Gellar expressed support for the idea.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats#cite_note-25)

**Juice Newton** (born **Judith Kay Newton**; February 18, 1952) is an American [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") and [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer, songwriter, and musician. Newton has received five [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") nominations in the Pop and Country Best Female Vocalist categories–winning once in 1983–as well as an [ACM Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Country_Music_Awards "Academy of Country Music Awards") for Top New Female Artist and two consecutive _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ Female Album Artist of the Year awards. Newton's other awards include a People's Choice Award for "Best Female Vocalist" and the Australian Music Media's "Number One International Country Artist".

Newton has several Gold and Platinum records to her credit, including _[Juice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice\_(Juice\_Newton\_album) "Juice (Juice Newton album)")_, _[Quiet Lies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiet\_Lies "Quiet Lies")_ and her first _Greatest Hits_ album. During the 1980s, she charted 14 top 10 hits across the _Billboard_[Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs"), [AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_(chart) "Adult Contemporary (chart)"), and [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") charts, with many of the recordings achieving crossover success and six of the songs hitting the No.1 position.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Juice_Newton&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Newton was born in [Lakehurst, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakehurst,_New_Jersey "Lakehurst, New Jersey").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-3) She is the daughter of a Navy officer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-people-4) Her mother encouraged her interest in music, giving her a guitar for her 13th birthday.

After graduating from [First Colonial High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Colonial_High_School "First Colonial High School") in [Virginia Beach, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Beach,_Virginia "Virginia Beach, Virginia"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-people-4) she attended [Foothill College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foothill_College "Foothill College") in [Los Altos Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Altos_Hills,_California "Los Altos Hills, California"). During this time, she performed [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") in some local coffeehouses. She then formed a [folk-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk-rock "Folk-rock") band with guitarist and songwriter [Otha Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otha_Young "Otha Young") and toured bars in Northern California with her band.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-AllMusic-5)

### Early music career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Juice_Newton&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early music career")]

In the early 1970s, Newton, [Otha Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otha_Young "Otha Young") and Tom Kealey formed a band that would eventually be called [Juice Newton & Silver Spur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton_&_Silver_Spur "Juice Newton & Silver Spur"), which was signed to [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records"). The group released two albums for RCA, in 1975 and 1976, but scored only one charting country single with "Love Is a Word". The band was dropped by RCA, then joined [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records") in 1977. The band broke up shortly after releasing just one more album.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-AllMusic-5)

In late 1977, Newton went solo, continuing to record for Capitol, and until 1982 Silver Spur remained the name of her backing band. Newton also sang backing vocals for three tracks on [Bob Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Welch_(musician) "Bob Welch (musician)")'s platinum solo debut album, including his hit "[Ebony Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebony_Eyes_(Bob_Welch_song) "Ebony Eyes (Bob Welch song)")".

Near the end of 1977, "[It's a Heartache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_a_Heartache "It's a Heartache")" became Newton's first solo record and a major hit in Mexico, where it was eventually certified Gold, and in 1978, she released it in the United States. “It’s a Heartache” was the first of Newton's eleven singles to chart on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). Also in 1978, [The Carpenters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carpenters "The Carpenters")' version of the Newton/Young-penned song "[Sweet, Sweet Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet,_Sweet_Smile "Sweet, Sweet Smile")" reached the Top 10 on both the Country and Adult Contemporary charts, and No. 44 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2) In 1978, Newton legally changed her name from "Judy Kay Newton" to "Juice Newton" ("Juice" having long been her nickname).

Newton's solo debut album, _Well Kept Secret_, was released later in 1978. Neither _Well Kept Secret_ nor its sole single, "Hey Baby", charted, but Capitol Records did renew Newton's contract. In 1979 Capitol's investment in Newton began to pay off as Newton had her first Top-40 Country hit with "Let's Keep It That Way" (another one-off single). Later that year, the album _[Take Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take\_Heart\_(Juice\_Newton\_album) "Take Heart (Juice Newton album)")_ featured five modestly charting singles: "Until Tonight", "[Any Way That You Want Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Any_Way_That_You_Want_Me "Any Way That You Want Me")", "You Fill My Life", "[Lay Back in the Arms of Someone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lay_Back_in_the_Arms_of_Someone "Lay Back in the Arms of Someone")", and "[Sunshine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunshine_(Jonathan_Edwards_song) "Sunshine (Jonathan Edwards song)")". In 1980, "Sunshine" became Newton's second top-40 country chart single, "You Fill My Life" reached No. 41, and "Until Tonight" was No. 42.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2) Both of Newton's initial solo efforts performed with modest success but failed to have lasting impacts on the album charts.

### Early 1980s pop music success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Juice_Newton&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early 1980s pop music success")]

In 1981, Newton's third solo album, simply titled _Juice_, was released. It spawned three consecutive Top-10 pop hits, namely "[Angel of the Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_of_the_Morning "Angel of the Morning")" (written by [Chip Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip_Taylor "Chip Taylor")), "[Queen of Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_Hearts_(Hank_DeVito_song)#Juice_Newton_version "Queen of Hearts (Hank DeVito song)")," and an updated version of "[The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known) "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)")" (the original version had appeared on the Silver Spur debut album), which earned Newton the first of several No. 1 Country chart singles. A fourth single, "[Ride 'Em Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ride_'Em_Cowboy_(song) "Ride 'Em Cowboy (song)")", from _Juice_ was released in 1984 to support Newton's first _Greatest Hits_ album, reaching the Billboard Country Top 40 chart.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2)

In 1981, Newton's video for "Angel of the Morning" was the first country-music video to air on MTV, the third by a female solo artist (after videos by [Pat Benatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Benatar "Pat Benatar") and [Carly Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carly_Simon "Carly Simon")), and the 40th to air on the channel overall.

_Juice_ sold more than a million copies in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and went Triple-Platinum (300,000 copies) in [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"). "Angel of the Morning" and "[The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sweetest_Thing_(I've_Ever_Known) "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)")" each reached No. 1 on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart, where Newton would chart regularly for the next several years. In 1982, Newton received two Grammy nominations for Best Female Vocalist: one for "Angel of the Morning" in the Pop category, and another for "Queen of Hearts" in Country.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-bio-6)

These two singles became her biggest sellers in the United States, each earning an [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") Gold certification. (In 1981 and 1982, when these singles were certified, the RIAA standard for Gold singles was "more than 1 million copies sold"; in 1989, RIAA lowered the standard to 500,000 for Gold single certifications.) The songs were also sizable hits in Canada, Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, and other countries. For example, "Angel of the Morning" peaked at No. 1 in Canada and No. 43 in the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") in 1981.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-British_Hit_Singles_&_Albums-7) While "The Sweetest Thing (I've Ever Known)" did not receive a U.S. certification, the song's popularity propelled album sales from Gold to Platinum, and the recording remained in the Top 40 (of the Hot 100) for 18 weeks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-bio-6) "Shot Full Of Love" was released as a single in the UK, but failed to chart.

In the spring of 1982 Newton released her fourth solo album, _[Quiet Lies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiet\_Lies "Quiet Lies")_, which sold 900,000 copies in the United States. The album went platinum in Canada (100,000 copies). It spawned the Top 10 Pop and Adult Contemporary hit "[Love's Been a Little Bit Hard on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love's_Been_a_Little_Bit_Hard_on_Me "Love's Been a Little Bit Hard on Me")" (which garnered her another Pop Female Vocalist Grammy nomination). "[Break It to Me Gently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break_It_to_Me_Gently "Break It to Me Gently")" was the second single and hit No. 1 on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart, No. 2 on the Billboard Country chart, as well as No. 9 in Cash Box and No. 11 on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). The recording, a contemporary remake of a [Brenda Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brenda_Lee "Brenda Lee") hit from the 1960s, won Newton her first [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") for Best Female Country Vocal Performance, beating out contemporaries [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton"), [Rosanne Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash"), [Emmylou Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmylou_Harris "Emmylou Harris") and [Sylvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_(singer) "Sylvia (singer)"). The album's third and final single, "Heart of the Night," reached No. 4 on the Adult Contemporary chart in early 1983 and climbed to No. 25 on the Hot 100.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2)

The album also garnered Newton an award from Australia as the "Top International Country Artist" for the continent. In 1982, Newton toured with country band [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_(American_band) "Alabama (American band)") on the "Salem Spirit" double-headliner tour. (Various acts opened for Newton and Alabama.)

The direction for Newton's sixth and final Capitol album, 1983's _Dirty Looks_, was decidedly more rock-oriented and experimental than her usual blending of folk, pop and country styles. The album spawned a moderate-sized hit with "Tell Her No" (Hot 100 No.27/AC No.14) and the title track, a rock-edged number that charted low in the Hot 100. The single "Stranger at My Door" had a brief run on the country chart. The album was a moderate success, selling more than 300,000 copies in the United States and going Gold in Canada (50,000 copies).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-8) (The song "Dirty Looks" was written by Dave Robbins and Van Stephenson, who would later become part of the Country group Blackhawk in the 1990s. The pair also wrote Newton's 1984 country single "Restless Heart.")

According to a 1984 front-page article in _Billboard_ magazine, changes at Capitol led Newton to return to RCA. The 1984 album _Can't Wait All Night_ continued with a rock-oriented sound. The launch single, "A Little Love," and the title track became Newton's final charting pop singles to date, reaching No.44 and No.66, respectively, while "Restless Heart" made No.57 on the country chart. "A Little Love" became Newton's seventh and final Top-10 hit on Billboard's Adult Contemporary chart, reaching the No.7 spot.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2) Newton's final double-header "Salem Spirit" tour with Alabama took place during this time, with Bill Medley of [The Righteous Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Righteous_Brothers "The Righteous Brothers") as the opening act.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-9)

### From pop to country

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Juice_Newton&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: From pop to country")]

Newton had always been moderately popular in country music; she responded to her waning popularity in the pop market by targeting her next album, 1985's _Old Flame_, solely to country audiences. The strategic move was a success; the album revitalized her career, reached No.12 on the Billboard album chart and featured six Top-10 country hits, including the No.1s "[You Make Me Want to Make You Mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Make_Me_Want_to_Make_You_Mine "You Make Me Want to Make You Mine")", "[Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurt_(Roy_Hamilton_song) "Hurt (Roy Hamilton song)")", and "[Both to Each Other](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends_and_Lovers_(Gloria_Loring_and_Carl_Anderson_song) "Friends and Lovers (Gloria Loring and Carl Anderson song)") (Friends and Lovers)" (with [Eddie Rabbitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Rabbitt "Eddie Rabbitt")), none of which (unlike her previous efforts) appeared at all on the pop charts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2) The duet was released to the public before the pop version "Friends and Lovers" by [Gloria Loring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Loring "Gloria Loring") and [Carl Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Anderson_(singer) "Carl Anderson (singer)"); the pop version was released to radio and stores two weeks after Newton and Rabbitt's version first appeared, even though it was recorded first. Newton's version was originally available only on a special edition of the _Old Flame_ album and on the Eddie Rabbitt album _Rabbitt Traxx_. The "Old Flame" album produced hit singles for more than sixteen months, with the final release being "What Can I Do with My Heart" (written by Otha Young), which reached the Top 10 in early 1987.

Newton returned to the Top 10 in 1988 with "Tell Me True" from her 1987 album _Emotion_. The album's lead single, the progressive-country tune "First Time Caller", stalled at No.24. Her final album of the decade, _Ain't Gonna Cry_ (1989), was not promoted by the label and did not chart. But it did spawn her final Top-40 country hit to date, "When Love Comes Around the Bend",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-charts-2) which RCA refused to release as a single because Newton's contract had not been renewed.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

After being dropped by RCA Records in 1989 (along with several other country artists, including [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton") and [Kenny Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Rogers "Kenny Rogers"), as country music as a whole was about to undergo momentous change), Newton took time to focus on her family life. Newton took a hiatus from recording albums, touring sporadically until returning to the music scene in late 1990s when she released the albums _[The Trouble with Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trouble\_with\_Angels\_(Juice\_Newton\_album) "The Trouble with Angels (Juice Newton album)")_ (1998) and _[American Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Girl\_(album) "American Girl (album)")_ (1999).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-disc-10)

### 1990s to present

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Juice_Newton&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1990s to present")]

In 1994, Newton contributed the track "Lovers of One Day" to an [Édith Piaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89dith_Piaf "Édith Piaf") tribute album which also included songs by [Pat Benatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Benatar "Pat Benatar") and [Donna Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Summer "Donna Summer").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-11)

In 1995, Newton recorded a double album of pop duets (which was slated to be sold via [infomercial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infomercial "Infomercial")), but the project was riddled with legal issues, resulting in a low-impact, "accidental" release of the "Platinum & Gold" series of duets in the early 2000s (the CD set was released without Newton's permission). Subsequently, bootleg CDs including most of the duets turned up on U.S. store shelves as _Gold & Platinum, Volumes 7 and 8_. Those CDs also contain 1995 solo versions of three of Newton's pop hits: "Angel of the Morning", "Love's Been a Little Bit Hard on Me" and "Queen of Hearts". Newton's duet partners included [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), [Melissa Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa_Manchester "Melissa Manchester"), [The Pointer Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pointer_Sisters "The Pointer Sisters") and [Frankie Valli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankie_Valli "Frankie Valli"). In 1998, Newton released _The Trouble with Angels_, a collection of seven re-recorded hits and three new songs, including the single "When I Get Over You". The 1998 effort was quickly followed by _American Girl_ in 1999, which was Newton's first album of all-new material since 1989 and featured the single "They Never Made It to Memphis". The collection featured tracks written by Otha Young, [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury"), [Nanci Griffith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanci_Griffith "Nanci Griffith"), [Tom Petty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Petty "Tom Petty") and Newton herself.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-12)

_[Every Road Leads Back to You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Every\_Road\_Leads\_Back\_to\_You "Every Road Leads Back to You")_ (which consists of live material and a bonus EP of four studio recordings of original songs) was released in 2002 with an accompanying DVD. _American Girl Vol. II_, which was originally sold exclusively at cdbaby.com and at Newton's live shows, was released in 2003 and reissued in 2006 and again in 2011 by Brookside Records.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-disc-10)

In 2005, Newton appeared on the TV show _[Hit Me, Baby, One More Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_Me,\_Baby,\_One\_More\_Time\_(TV\_series) "Hit Me, Baby, One More Time (TV series)")_, on which she performed a folk-rock rendition of "[Pieces Of Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieces_of_Me_(Ashlee_Simpson_song) "Pieces of Me (Ashlee Simpson song)")" and a truncated version of "Queen of Hearts"; online voters selected Newton's performance as their favorite of the five acts that appeared on the episode.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-13) In the mid-2000s, Newton also contributed tracks to the albums _An All-Star Tribute To [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher")_ ("Reason to Believe") and _An All-Star Tribute to [Shania Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shania\_Twain "Shania Twain")_ ("Come On Over").

On November 15, 2007, Newton released _The Gift of Christmas_, her first Christmas album.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-14) The 12-song album includes a new version of Newton's "Christmas Needs Love to Be Christmas" and "[Mary's Boy Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary's_Boy_Child "Mary's Boy Child")", as well as a special Christmas version of "For Believers", an Otha Young-penned song first recorded in 1983 for the _Dirty Looks_ album.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/JuiceNewtonByPhilKonstantin.jpg/250px-JuiceNewtonByPhilKonstantin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JuiceNewtonByPhilKonstantin.jpg)

Juice Newton, San Diego, 2009

On August 6, 2009, Newton's longtime musical partner Otha Young died of cancer. The pair worked together for 37 years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-15)

In 2010, Newton's _Duets: Friends & Memories_ album was released by Fuel 2000.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-16) The album contained duets performed with [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), [Melissa Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa_Manchester "Melissa Manchester"), [Frankie Valli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankie_Valli "Frankie Valli") and others. One single ("Funny How Time Slips Away") was released.

In 2011, Fuel 2000 released _Juice Newton: The Ultimate Hits Collection_, which included her own version of the Carpenters' 1978 hit "Sweet Sweet Smile", which Newton and Otha Young wrote in the '70s.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-17)

In 2012, BGO Records issued a two-CD set containing Newton's three 1970s Capitol albums: _Come To Me_, _Well Kept Secret_ and _Take Heart_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-18) This marked the first time these albums have been available in the CD format. With the release of this set, all Newton's 17 studio albums have been issued on CD.

In the 2016 film _[Deadpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_(film) "Deadpool (film)")_, Newton's version of "Angel of the Morning" was used for the opening credits montage.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-19) As a result, the track re-charted on the Billboard Country chart, reaching No. 43, and also hit No. 3 on Spotify's World Music chart. In 2020, Newton's version of "Angel of the Morning" was featured in the film _[Promising Young Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promising\_Young\_Woman "Promising Young Woman")_.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Juice_Newton&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Newton bought a thoroughbred [gelding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelding "Gelding") named Puppy in 1983[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-people-4) and stabled him at the [Los Angeles Equestrian Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Equestrian_Center "Los Angeles Equestrian Center"). The center's manager was [polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polo "Polo") star and coach Tom Goodspeed. Newton married Goodspeed in 1985. They have two children: Jessica and Tyler.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-people-4)

Besides continuing in the music business, Newton works as a horse trader, dealing mostly in European breeds.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-20) She also played polo herself.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_Newton#cite_note-people-4)
